questions.question:

questions.solution:

• In the given sentence, the correct verb to use is 'owes' because it accurately completes the sentence meaningfully.

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

We believe that visiting Shimla is the better therapy for you.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the first part of the given sentence, the use of 'the better therapy' is incorrect.
 
• The correct phrase should be 'the best therapy' since 'better' is used for comparison between two things, while 'best' is used when comparing more than two or when no comparison is being made.
 
• **Example:** *We believe that visiting Shimla is the best therapy for you*.

Hence, the correct statement is** "*We believe that visiting Shimla is the best therapy __for you*."**

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Please distribute these balloons between all the candidates.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase 'these balloons between' is incorrect because the preposition 'between' is used for two entities, but 'all the candidates' implies more than two.
 
• The correct preposition in this context should be 'among' which is used for more than two entities.

Hence, the correct sentence is **"*Please distribute these balloons among __all the candidates*."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The preposition 'between' is used when referring to two people or things.
 
• The preposition 'among' is used when referring to more than two people or things.
 
• Example: *The secret was shared **between** the two friends.*
 
• Example: *The secret was shared **among** the group of friends.*

Hence, the correct statement is **"*I read the directions, but I still can't figure out__ how it works*."**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

The trio of women at the table ________ representative of the enormous flux of American life.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'was'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "The trio of women" is a collective noun that is singular in form and takes a singular verb.
 
• Even though "women" is plural, the subject "trio" is singular, necessitating a singular verb form.
 
• The context of the sentence suggests a simple past tense scenario.
 
• "Was" correctly matches the singular collective noun "trio" and the simple past tense context.
 
• Using "was" makes the sentence clear and grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 (had being): Grammatically incorrect; the phrase "had being" is not a valid verb form.
 
• Option 3 (has been): Incorrect tense; "has been" is present perfect, not consistent with the simple past needed here.
 
• Option 4 (were): Incorrect verb form; "were" is plural, whereas "trio" is singular.
